subject: Afonso - connect/ Abbvie, Philips and frontier voice ai labs
text:

noticed the planned EU and US expansion of LOLA so thought I'd reach out to

I lead the voice AI team here at Encord and we've been working with several
frontier AI teams (inc. Kyutai, Udio) and medical teams like Abbvie,

explainable and clinically correct datasets.

subject: Thoughts for LandingAI
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been following LandingAI's work on agentic document extraction -
impressive how you're tackling complex, real-world docs in production.

Once document AI is live, the bottleneck shifts from extraction accuracy to
reliably surfacing failures - layout drift, OCR ambiguity, multilingual
edge cases.

Closing that loop back into training and eval, without burning engineering
cycles, is where things get hard.

Curious how your team is thinking about this as ADE scales - would you be
open to connecting next week?

subject: Thoughts for [COMPANY]
text:

subject: Scalpel Ltd.'s AI Pipeline
text:
[NAME], 

There's a pattern we keep seeing with ML teams at your stage: engineers burning sprint cycles on a pipeline stage that isn't the actual constraint. 

Labeling is usually the first thing to get attention; it's measurable, the team can point to output, and it's easy to staff up. But when we map the pipeline, the real throughput bottleneck is in curation or validation far more often than anyone expects. Model performance doesn't move. Nobody can explain why. 

We built a diagnostic that identifies which stage it actually is for your setup; maps across curation, labeling, QA, and validation, and generates a fix-priority report. 

If that's useful, I'll send it over.
